claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser melting can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Controlled porosity introduced by SLM will reduce the bulk density of HfMoTaTiZr.
An optimized pore size and pore distribution can provide a porous HfMoTaTiZr microstructure.
The porous material can retain sufficient load-bearing cross-sectional area to preserve mechanical strength.
Solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion are inherent strengthening mechanisms in HfMoTaTiZr.
Solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion will remain effective after controlled porosity is introduced.
SLM processing can produce a high-entropy alloy with outstanding room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
Reducing the density of a refractory high-entropy alloy while retaining strong high-temperature properties is feasible.
Porous SLM-processed HfMoTaTiZr will retain mechanical strength with only minimal loss relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed strength retention applies from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposed behavior applies under both tensile and compressive loading.
A tensile-strength reduction greater than 20% at room temperature or elevated temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed and the mechanism says strength will be preserved, whereas the predicted outcome permits a minimal loss and the rejection rule permits a tensile-strength loss of up to 20%.
